chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Asama, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The believer is not tested with anything more difficult for him than three characteristics from which he is deprived.' It was said, 'And what are they?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Equalizing in what is in his hand (generosity/spending), and fairness with himself (self-restraint), and remembering Allah frequently. Indeed, I do not mean (merely saying) 'Glory be to Allah' and 'Praise be to Allah' and 'There is no god but Allah', but rather remembering Allah when what is permissible comes to him, and remembering Allah when what is prohibited comes to him.'

key_terms.الْمُوَاسَاةُ: Equalizing or being generous with one's wealth/resources

ai.seo_question: What are the three difficult characteristics a believer is tested with according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights that the most arduous trials for a believer are generosity (*muwasat*), self-restraint (*insaf*), and constant God-consciousness (*dhikr*). He distinguishes true *dhikr* from mere formulaic recitation, defining it as the active awareness of God in both permissible (*halal*) and prohibited (*haram*) actions, a concept central to Shia ethical jurisprudence. This emphasizes that spiritual depth is measured by consistent mindfulness across all dimensions of life, not just ritual performance.
